The Great Cloud of Witnesses
WIT-ness-es
noun phrase
From the Greek nephos martyron, “cloud of witnesses,” the great company of the faithful of old who bear testimony to the life of faith.

Biblical Definition

The great cloud of witnesses is the host of the faithful saints of old, named and unnamed in the eleventh chapter of Hebrews, who having lived and died in faith bear testimony to the believer that the race may be run and won. Wherefore, says the apostle, seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us (Heb 12:1). The dictionary marks the figure rightly. These witnesses are not spectators in heaven peering down upon the saints below, as the unwary suppose, but witnesses in the older and truer sense: men who by their faith bore witness, who obtained a good report through faith (Heb 11:39), and whose recorded lives testify that God is faithful to them that trust Him. By faith Abel offered, by faith Enoch was translated, by faith Abraham obeyed; and all these, having obtained a good report, received not the promise, God having provided some better thing for us (Heb 11:40). So the Scripture sets them before the believer as a great host of testimony, that he run not as one alone but in the company of all the faithful who have proved the way. Their witness is an encouragement to lay aside every weight and to press on, looking past them to Jesus, the author and finisher of faith, in whom alone the race is finished.

Webster 1828 Definition

The great company of the faithful of old whose lives bear witness that the life of faith may be run and won.

CLOUD OF WITNESSES, the host of the faithful saints of old.

They are the men of faith named in the eleventh chapter of Hebrews.

They are witnesses who bore testimony, not mere spectators in heaven.

They obtained a good report through faith and proved God faithful.

Their witness encourages the believer to lay aside every weight and run.

Key Scripture

Heb 12:1 — "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,"

Heb 11:39 — "And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:"

Heb 11:40 — "God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect."

Heb 11:13 — "These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth."

Modern Corruption

A glory of the faith little redefined; it recovers the saints of old as witnesses by their faith, not spectators of ours.

expand to see more

The great cloud of witnesses has drawn little redefinition from the present age, though it is often read amiss, as if the dead watched the living from heaven. The dictionary records it that the reader may know these as witnesses in the truer sense, men whose faith bore testimony that God is faithful to them that trust Him.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the faithful of old testify to us by their lives. They are not an audience of departed spirits but a host of witnesses who, by faith, obtained a good report; and their recorded endurance encourages the believer that the race may be run and won. So the saint runs not alone nor untried, but in the company of all who have gone before and proved the way, laying aside every weight and looking past them to Jesus, in whom alone the race is finished.

Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “cloud of witnesses,” the phrase names the faithful of old who bear testimony to faith.

Cloud of Witnesses — Greek nephos martyron, “cloud of witnesses.”

It is the host of the faithful saints named in Hebrews eleven.

They obtained a good report and proved God faithful.

Their witness encourages the believer to run with patience.
